subject: microbiology
title: McFadyean Reaction, Medusa Head Colonies and Bacillus cereus

steps.tx: The **McFadyean reaction** stains anthrax blood smears with polychrome methylene blue: capsule appears as amorphous purple pink material around blue boxcar rods, demonstrating the polypeptide capsule in vivo (lost often in culture), a field test from veterinary anthrax work where carcass blood was the specimen.
steps.say: Purple capsule clouds around blue rods in blood: McFadyean names anthrax in the field.

left.title: Reaction mechanics
points: Bacilli: dark blue, square ended chains
Best in fresh carcass or patient blood films

steps.tx: The **McFadyean reaction** uses polychrome methylene blue on anthrax blood smears. The capsule appears as amorphous purple pink material around blue boxcar rods, showing the polypeptide capsule that forms in the animal. Culture often loses that capsule. The method comes from veterinary field work in which carcass blood was the specimen, naming anthrax before a full laboratory culture returned.
steps.say: Polychrome methylene blue paints anthrax capsules as purple pink clouds around blue boxcar rods in blood. The polypeptide capsule is an in vivo feature often lost in culture. Carcass blood made this a field test.

vis.alt: A blood film stained with polychrome methylene blue shows blue rods surrounded by purple pink capsular material.
vis.caption: Polychrome methylene blue shows blue anthrax rods ringed by amorphous purple pink capsule in a blood film. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Medusa head colonies** of anthracis on blood agar are large, grey, rough colonies with comma shaped outgrowths like a Medusa's hair (curled projections), non haemolytic, ground glass, sticky; inverted fir tree growth in gelatin stab and penicillin susceptibility (string of pearls test) complete classical identification before referral.
steps.say: Rough grey Medusa heads that do not haemolyse: colonial portrait of anthracis.

left.title: Colony portrait
points: Ground glass, tenacious (stands like beaten egg white)
Medusa head projections at low magnification

right.title: Classical tests
points: String of pearls on penicillin agar
Cereus: motile, haemolytic, penicillin resistant usually

steps.tx: **Bacillus cereus** (motile, beta haemolytic, penicillin resistant spore cousin) causes two food poisonings (next lesson details), anthrax like pneumonia in metal workers by cereus carrying anthrax plasmids (B cereus biovar anthracis borderland), eye infections after trauma, and device and wound infections, identification by the anthracis negatives above.
steps.say: Same genus, opposite habits: cereus moves, haemolyses and shrugs penicillin.

left.title: Cereus identity
points: Large rods, spores central not swelling
MYEP selective media for food counts

right.title: Cereus disease
points: Anthrax like pneumonia rare plasmid strains

steps.tx: **Selective Bacillus media** (PLET and MYEP, polymyxin egg yolk mannitol bromothymol) isolate cereus group from food and environmental samples while suppressing rivals, spore counts after heat shock measure the spore load directly. Food microbiology quantifies what clinical benches only name.
steps.say: Heat shock counts spores, egg yolk reads lecithinase: food Bacillus work is quantitative.

left.title: Media design
points: Heat shock 70 to 80 degrees selects spores

right.title: Food investigation
points: Counts above 10^5 per gram support cereus

steps.tx: **Spore germination in food** explains cereus outbreaks: spores survive rice boiling, germinate as rice cools slowly, vegetative cells make toxin (in gut for diarrhoeal, in food for emetic cereulide), reheating fries rice but cereulide survives frying. Time and temperature, not final cooking, decide safety.
steps.say: Boiled rice left warm is a germination incubator; frying cannot destroy cereulide.

nodes.label: Cells grow, cereulide forms in food

steps.tx: **Other Bacillus species** (subtilis food spoilage and opportunist, licheniformis food poisoning, thuringiensis insecticide and occasional human infection) mostly contaminate cultures innocently; repeated sterile site isolation and device contexts promote them, susceptibility usually broad except cereus group beta lactam resistance. In suspected anthrax events that distinction also has forensic consequences, which is another reason isolates leave the local laboratory quickly.
steps.say: A single Bacillus in blood is dust; the same in three bottles is a consultation.

steps.tx: **Anthrax versus cereus arbitration** in a modern laboratory ends at reference level: MALDI cannot reliably separate cereus group, toxin gene and plasmid PCR can, biosafety and legal stakes forbid local improvisation with suspected anthracis beyond safe referral. Notify, package, refer is an identification result too.
steps.say: Cereus group on MALDI plus exposure history equals referral, not local heroics.

left.title: Local bench limits
points: Blood culture rods plus exposure escalates
Stop work and notify by protocol

steps.tx: **String of pearls test** (anthracis growing as swollen bead chains on low penicillin agar, cell wall injured) and penicillin susceptibility together were pre molecular arbitration, still viva favourites because they hinge on anthracis's unusual beta lactam tenderness in a resistant genus.
steps.say: Penicillin swells anthracis into pearls while cereus grows on: susceptibility as morphology.

left.title: Pearl test
points: Low dose penicillin agar (0.05 units traditions)

right.title: Therapeutic echo
points: Penicillin once anthrax therapy (susceptible natural strains)
